confirmed_invariants: INV-1 issuance locality: the only create_grant/create_approval requests in the desktop codebase are inside run_local_mission (desktop/src-tauri/src/mission_runner.rs:830-843, progress marker 845-848); run_local_mission is invoked solely by the run_mission Tauri command (desktop/src-tauri/src/lib.rs:493-497) whose registered surface (lib.rs:629-639) contains no other Core-touching command — draft_mission (mission_runner.rs draft_local_mission), compile_mission (preflight_local_mission), and load_replay never open the Core socket; the reviewed-digest gate (mission_runner.rs:740-745) executes before any Core process is started (CoreProcess start at 823), and desktop/src-tauri/tests/mission_execution.rs:255-278 proves a mismatched reviewed digest refuses before a lane exists. The daemon additionally gates issuance to PLANNING state with exact field counts (nemesis_core_daemon.adb:257-259, 294-296).

INV-2 digest binding without widening: reviewed_action_digest must equal mission.action_digest (mission_runner.rs:743-745); create_approval carries mission.action_digest (mission_runner.rs:838-843); the daemon persists the approval under a digest-keyed filename (authority_store.adb:56-61) with overwrite refusal ('approval_already_exists', authority_store.adb:396-403) so a consumed approval can never be re-armed; authorize_action loads by exact digest with mission+digest cross-check on parse (authority_store.adb:412-449) and the SPARK kernel refuses any digest inequality (nemesis-kernel-approvals.adb:24-27, Post at nemesis-kernel-approvals.ads:31-40); the worker's proposal is checked against the reviewed relative_path and content_digest before authorization is requested (mission_runner.rs:886-903) and the executed write is the reviewed replacement bytes themselves (mission_runner.rs:936-940, verified 981-987).

INV-3 refusal propagation: any non-OK Core response becomes MissionRunError::Refused embedding the full response JSON including decision and reason (mission_runner.rs:682-685); Display is the raw message (mission_runner.rs:33-41); run_mission converts it to a typed CommandFailure with code/message/recovery (lib.rs:62-92) and both records it in the polled snapshot and returns it as the command error (lib.rs run_mission Err arm); App.tsx surfaces code, message, and recovery in a role=alert block, asserted by App.test.tsx 'renders typed refusal and concrete recovery guidance'.

INV-4 UI claims are enforced copy: 'ONE-SHOT · EXACT ACTION DIGEST' (AuthorityReview.tsx:71-74) ← nemesis-kernel-approvals.adb:11-31 (consumed→Approval_Replayed; exact digest equality) plus durable consumption before the authorization event (nemesis_core_daemon.adb:408-437) and anti-re-arm persistence (authority_store.adb:396-403); 'PARENT GRANT → ATTENUATED CHILD' (AuthorityReview.tsx:76-80) ← persisted parent load with fail-closed missing/corrupt/inactive handling (nemesis_core_daemon.adb:361-384), SPARK-proved Derive_Child_Grant postcondition (nemesis-kernel-capabilities.ads:83-107, body .adb:43-58) and runtime Is_Attenuation re-check (nemesis_core_daemon.adb:385-399); 'Consumed exactly once … replay is refused' (AuthorityReview.tsx:100-103) ← same consumption path plus replay refusal proven across restart in tests; footer 'backend re-reads the file and refuses any changed byte before creating a lane' (AuthorityReview.tsx:113-116) ← contract re-read (lib.rs:481), digest gate (mission_runner.rs:740-745), expectedSha256/baseRevision workspace validation (mission_runner.rs:454-459) all before lane creation (mission_runner.rs:769). App.test.tsx:216-222 additionally pins that the digests shown in review are the exact values passed to run_mission.

INV-5 probe/test strength: run_vertical_slice.py raises on any non-zero subprocess (run(), lines 59-72) and on any non-OK Core response (expect(), 158-162); the replay probe (321-333) re-issues authorize_action after a daemon restart and hard-fails unless status==REFUSED AND reason==approval_replayed — a fail-open regression (OK/AUTHORIZED) or a reason drift both raise. test_daemon_api.py test_authority_is_persisted_one_shot_and_fail_closed (277-392) asserts exact status/decision/reason triples for: missing grant (no_parent_grant), missing approval (no_approval), duplicate issuance (grant_already_exists/approval_already_exists), replay before AND after daemon restart (approval_replayed), on-disk approval tamper (approval_corrupt), on-disk grant tamper (grant_corrupt), and PLANNING-only issuance; test_lifecycle (262-273) asserts terminal-state authorize_action refuses without sequence movement.

INV-6 (field counts + state gates): Exact_Fields counts match the documented commands exactly — ping 2, create 7, authorize 4, run 3, inspect 3, create_grant 4, create_approval 5, authorize_action 7, action_completed 5, accept_evidence 6, propose_completion 3, receipt_payload 3 (nemesis_core_daemon.adb:161, 166, 220, 246, 258, 295, 333, 452, 471, 497, 542); state gates match: issuance PLANNING-only (258-259, 295-296), authorize_action/action_completed/accept_evidence/propose_completion RUNNING-only (333-334, 452-453, 472-473, 497-498), receipt_payload COMPLETE with current claims (542-545); message bound 65,536 both sides (nemesis-core-json.ads:2, mission_runner.rs:22); socket chmod 0600 after bind and home 0700 (nemesis_core_daemon.adb daemon prologue) match the doc; all documented refusal reasons exist verbatim in code (nemesis_core_daemon.adb:106-131).

INV-4: AuthorityReview's new claims (ONE-SHOT / EXACT ACTION DIGEST / PARENT GRANT → ATTENUATED CHILD / consumed exactly once) are enforced by shipped code, not aspirational copy
INV-5: The vertical-slice replay probe and the daemon-api hostile tests actually fail if replay were accepted (assertion strength catches a fail-open regression)
INV-6a: protocols/local-core-v1.md matches implemented field counts and state gates
INV-6b: protocols/local-core-v1.md matches implemented refusal vocabulary and recovery/durability behavior

gaps.evidence: protocols/local-core-v1.md:64 vs daemon/src/nemesis-core-mission_store.adb:484-513 and tests/integration/test_daemon_api.py:394-420 (test comment explicitly: 'never brick to STORE_CORRUPT').
gaps.impact: The sentence 'Ledger/checkpoint disagreement returns corrupt state; Core does not guess or run' is only true for a checkpoint AHEAD of the ledger (daemon/src/nemesis-core-mission_store.adb:486-491 → Store_Corrupt). A missing or lagging checkpoint is deliberately rebuilt from the hash-chain-validated ledger tail (nemesis-core-mission_store.adb:495-513, SQL-001), and tests/integration/test_daemon_api.py:394-420 asserts that recovery. A maintainer 'fixing' code to match the doc would reintroduce the SQL-001 crash-brick.
gaps.precondition: A maintainer or reviewer relies on the protocol document for Core recovery semantics.
gaps.remediation: Reword the Recovery paragraph to distinguish the two directions: checkpoint ahead of the ledger fails closed as corrupt; checkpoint missing/behind is rebuilt from the authoritative ledger.

gaps.impact: The documented refusal vocabulary says decisions are 'REFUSED_CAPABILITY or REFUSED_APPROVAL' each with a reason, but the post-consumption capability check can return REFUSED_BUDGET (kernel/src/nemesis-kernel-capabilities.adb:18-19), emitted verbatim via Authority_Decision'Image with NO reason key (daemon/src/nemesis_core_daemon.adb:428-434). Consumers parsing per the doc would meet an undocumented decision value and a missing field.
gaps.precondition: A direct local socket client sends authorize_action with estimated_bytes exceeding the 4096-byte parent budget (the desktop client cannot: replacement_bytes ≤ maxWriteBytes 4096 is enforced at contract compile).
gaps.remediation: Document REFUSED_BUDGET (and that the Authorize-refusal branch carries decision only), or add a reason string to that branch for uniformity.

gaps.evidence: tests/integration/test_daemon_api.py:277-392 (all attempt() calls use matching WORKER/SCOPE and estimated_bytes 128); daemon/src/nemesis_core_daemon.adb:352-434; kernel/tests/nemesis_authority_tests.adb:122-160.
gaps.impact: The hostile daemon-API tests cover missing/tampered authority, one-shot replay across restart, and PLANNING-only issuance, but never exercise the post-consumption Authorize refusal dimensions through the socket: scope_digest mismatch, worker_id mismatch, estimated_bytes over the 4096 parent budget, or grant/approval expiry. These are asserted only at the kernel unit level (kernel/tests/nemesis_authority_tests.adb:122-160), which would not catch a daemon-layer request-to-Action_Request wiring regression. The documented 'a later budget or scope failure has already burned its one-shot approval' fail-closed direction (protocols/local-core-v1.md:41-43) is also untested end-to-end.
gaps.precondition: A future daemon-layer regression in how authorize_action populates Action_Request (e.g., taking scope or subject from the stored grant instead of the request), or in window/budget wiring.
gaps.remediation: Add daemon-level cases: wrong scope_digest, wrong worker_id, estimated_bytes 4097 — each asserting status REFUSED and that a subsequent exact retry reports approval_replayed (proving the approval burned on the failed attempt).

gaps.impact: protocols/local-core-v1.md:58-62 claims authority records are written 'tmp-then-rename with F_FULLFSYNC on file and directory', but Full_Sync_Directory (authority_store.adb:38-47) discards both the open and fcntl results, and Write_Record (authority_store.adb:147-151) treats directory sync as best-effort after rename — only file-level F_FULLFSYNC failure fails closed (137-142). The code is therefore weaker than the documented durability contract. Practical replay exposure is judged unlikely because the subsequent Action_Authorized ledger commit performs its own F_FULLFSYNC (device-wide cache flush) after Persist_Consumed_Approval returns (daemon/src/nemesis_core_daemon.adb:415-437) [INFERENCE on macOS flush ordering], but the doc states a guarantee the code does not enforce.
gaps.precondition: Directory F_FULLFSYNC fails or is skipped (open/fcntl error) immediately followed by power loss after the consumed-approval rename.
gaps.remediation: Propagate Full_Sync_Directory failure so Write_Record reports failure (mapped to Authority_IO_Failure, which authorize_action already fails closed on), or soften the doc to 'best-effort directory flush ordered before the ledger commit's full device flush'.

gaps.impact: run_local_mission validates the worker proposal's method, relative_path, and content_digest (mission_runner.rs:886-903) but not its action_kind or purpose fields, whereas scripts/run_vertical_slice.py:296-302 compares the full params object. No authority widening is possible: the lane write is performed by the runner itself with the reviewed replacement bytes (write_lane_file at mission_runner.rs:936-940), the content verifier re-reads them (mission_runner.rs:981-987), and authorization uses mission.action_digest, which already binds kind 'filesystem.modify' from the reviewed normalized action (desktop/src-tauri/src/production.rs:208-214). Recorded only as a strength-parity note.
gaps.precondition: None required; observation of differing check strength between the shipped runner and the slice probe.
gaps.remediation: Optionally mirror the slice's full-params comparison in the runner for defense in depth.

findings.title: Lane report: nemesis.hardening-audit.result/v1 (protocol_clients)

evidence.excerpt: Ledger/checkpoint disagreement returns corrupt state; Core does not guess or run.
evidence.explanation: The Recovery section states disagreement always yields corrupt state.
evidence.label: Doc claim

evidence.excerpt: if Checkpoint_Status = Checkpoint_Valid and then Checkpoint.Sequence > Recovered.Sequence then Result := Store_Corrupt; ... Rebuild the derived checkpoint from the ledger tail whenever it is missing or stale
evidence.explanation: Only checkpoint-ahead fails closed; lagging/mismatched checkpoints are rebuilt from the authoritative ledger tail (SQL-001 comment at nemesis-core-mission_store.adb:495-497).
evidence.label: Implementation

optionalProperties.remediation: Reword to distinguish checkpoint-ahead (fail closed, corrupt) from checkpoint-behind/missing (rebuilt from authoritative ledger).

findings.summary: protocols/local-core-v1.md:64 says 'Ledger/checkpoint disagreement returns corrupt state; Core does not guess or run', but the implementation fails closed only when the checkpoint is AHEAD of the ledger; a missing/lagging checkpoint is rebuilt from the hash-chain-validated ledger (SQL-001), and the integration test asserts that recovery. A maintainer aligning code to the doc would reintroduce the crash-brick.
findings.title: Protocol doc overstates checkpoint-disagreement behavior vs SQL-001 rebuild-on-lag implementation

evidence.excerpt: return Context_Response ("REFUSED", Context, "," & Quote & "decision" & Quote & ":" & Quote & Authority_Decision'Image (Decision) & Quote);
evidence.explanation: The Authorize-refusal path returns only the decision image, unlike every other refusal which includes a reason.
evidence.label: Reason-less branch

optionalProperties.remediation: Document REFUSED_BUDGET and the decision-only shape of this branch, or add a reason string for uniformity.

findings.summary: The doc enumerates authorize_action refusal decisions as REFUSED_CAPABILITY or REFUSED_APPROVAL, each paired with a reason. The post-consumption Authorize call can also return REFUSED_BUDGET, which the daemon emits verbatim with no reason key. Reachable only by a direct socket client sending estimated_bytes > 4096; the desktop client cannot produce it.
findings.title: Refusal vocabulary omits reachable REFUSED_BUDGET decision (emitted without a reason field)

evidence.excerpt: return self.request("authorize_action", mission_id=mission_id, worker_id=WORKER, scope_digest=SCOPE, action_digest=ACTION, estimated_bytes=128)
evidence.explanation: All daemon-level authorize_action attempts send worker_id=WORKER, scope_digest=SCOPE, estimated_bytes=128 — never a mismatching subject/scope or an over-budget size — so Authorize's Refused_Capability/Refused_Budget branches are never traversed through the socket API.
evidence.label: Uniform happy inputs

optionalProperties.remediation: Add daemon-level cases for wrong scope_digest, wrong worker_id, and estimated_bytes 4097, each asserting REFUSED and that an exact retry then reports approval_replayed (proving the approval burned closed).

findings.summary: test_daemon_api.py covers replay, missing authority, tamper, and state gating with exact assertions, but every attempt() uses matching worker/scope and in-budget bytes. Scope mismatch, worker mismatch, over-budget, and expiry refusals — and the documented rule that a request failing the later capability check has already burned its one-shot approval — are only covered by kernel unit asserts, which would miss a daemon-layer Action_Request wiring regression.
findings.title: Daemon-API hostile tests skip post-consumption Authorize dimensions (scope/worker/budget/expiry) and the burned-approval-on-late-failure direction

evidence.excerpt: FD := C_Open (...); if FD >= 0 then Ignore := Fcntl (FD, F_FULLFSYNC); Ignore := C_Close (FD); end if;
evidence.explanation: Both the fcntl and close results are assigned to a throwaway variable; an open failure silently skips the flush entirely.
evidence.label: Ignored result

optionalProperties.remediation: Propagate Full_Sync_Directory failure into Write_Record's Success (mapping to Authority_IO_Failure, on which authorize_action already fails closed), or soften the doc wording.

findings.summary: Full_Sync_Directory discards open/fcntl failures, making the directory flush best-effort, while protocols/local-core-v1.md:58-62 states authority records get F_FULLFSYNC on file AND directory. File-level fsync failure fails closed; directory-level does not. Practical replay exposure is judged unlikely (the later ledger commit's F_FULLFSYNC flushes the device cache after consumption persists — [INFERENCE] on macOS flush ordering), but the code enforces less than the doc guarantees.
findings.title: Directory F_FULLFSYNC result ignored while doc claims full-sync 'on file and directory'
